text:
Evidence supports testing persistent-interest pooling, but does not establish that recurrence-weighted cosine support beats recency weighting. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) attends more locally on sparse datasets and more broadly on dense datasets; these attention patterns do not demonstrate persistent interests causally. [Personalized-popularity research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04329) finds repeated listening useful in music, but repeat-consumption evidence transfers imperfectly to unseen-item Amazon recommendation.

Popularity and embedding geometry are plausible confounds. [DirectMag](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457323003436) finds that item-vector magnitude captures substantial popularity information; cosine normalization removes this magnitude channel, but its accuracy tradeoffs depend on learned angular structure. [Popularity-amplification analysis](https://zhoushengisnoob.github.io/papers/WSDM25.pdf) finds popularity strongly represented in the principal spectrum of recommendation scores. Neither result directly proves that cosine-history aggregation exploits dense clusters in this task. Nevertheless, mathematically, items similar to many unrelated histories can receive high aggregate support without personalized relevance.

Suggested controls—not established findings: compare uniform, recency-only, and recurrence-aware pooling using identical histories, embeddings, and normalized weight sums; include a train-frequency-only score and frequency-matched shuffled histories. Measure support correlations with log training frequency and candidate mean cosine to random catalog items; subtract that background cosine as a density control. Report validation gains within target-frequency bins and after controlling both frequency and density. Deduplicate history items or cap repeated contributions to separate recurrence from multiplicity. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged and select by four-category macro HR@10. Gains surviving these controls would strengthen the persistent-interest interpretation; aggregate gains alone cannot establish it.
